purpose: Evidence register for a terrain-based Sofia pluvial-flood screening map; not a validated flood probability, flood depth, damage or loss model.

sources.title: Sofia Municipality Strategic Security Vision 2024–2030
sources.locator: Section 3.16, printed page 11 / PDF page 11; footnote 13 refers to the National Risk Profile adopted 4 January 2023.
findings: The municipality identifies urban rain-driven flooding associated with intense precipitation as a major local risk and also identifies infrastructure-related flooding as possible.
supports: Local relevance of pluvial flood screening

sources.title: A Depression-Based Index to Represent Topographic Control in Urban Pluvial Flooding
sources.authors: Huang, H.; Chen, X.; Wang, X.; Wang, X.; Liu, L.
findings: Depression storage, contributing catchments and catchment slope are relevant terrain controls; their proposed TCI is ln(A*sqrt(S)/V), using depression catchment area A, dimensionless catchment mean slope S and depression storage volume V.
Its Guangzhou case study found depression-based TCI more useful than cell-based TWI; this does not establish transferable thresholds for Sofia.
The authors distinguish topographic control from actual flood risk. Their resolution experiment found greater instability for small depressions and coarser grids.
supports: Do not call terrain-only scores actual risk
does_not_support: A scientifically established weighted sum of local fill depth, local slope and contributing area
Treating fill depth as storm flood depth

sources.title: Risk of flooding from surface water – understanding and using the map
findings: Operational surface-water hazard mapping combines terrain with rainfall, runoff losses, drainage assumptions and hydraulic simulation; local and historical evidence are used for review.
The model accounts for buildings and distinguishes modelled depth and annual exceedance likelihood.
supports: Rainfall and drainage are required for event or probability claims
does_not_support: Transferring England drainage rates or rainfall return periods to Sofia

sources.title: Using Selective Drainage Methods to Extract Continuous Surface Flow from 1-Meter Lidar-Derived Digital Elevation Data
sources.authors: Poppenga, S.K.; Worstell, B.B.; Stoker, J.M.; Greenlee, S.K.
findings: Roads, railways and other obstructions can create depressions in high-resolution elevation models. Filling without representing drainage through obstructions can produce an incorrect spill location and surface-flow route.
supports: Separate geometric fill depth from observed inundation
does_not_support: Assuming all identified depressions are genuine
Assuming all culverts are captured by the municipal DTM

sources.title: Sendai Framework terminology: Disaster risk
sources.publisher: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
findings: Disaster risk depends on hazard, exposure, vulnerability and capacity, with potential losses considered over a time period.
supports: Separate terrain screening from asset exposure and loss risk
does_not_support: Calling a terrain rank expected damage or annual flood risk

sources.title: Sendai Framework terminology: Exposure
sources.publisher: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
findings: Exposure describes people, infrastructure and other assets located in hazard-prone areas; vulnerability and capacity are further inputs to quantitative risk.
supports: Use infrastructure overlap as exposure context
does_not_support: Inferring asset vulnerability or damage from point locations alone

sources.title: OpenStreetMap mapped open-water footprints: natural=water and water=river
sources.locator: Water=river describes the river water area; natural=water describes mapped water surfaces. Local snapshot and feature IDs are retained in data/reference.
findings: The hidden exclusion uses the interiors of actual mapped water polygons on the aligned 5 m grid, including multipolygon holes.
Explicitly intermittent, seasonal, dry, disused, covered or indoor objects are excluded from this permanent-water mask; unbuffered waterway centrelines are not water footprints.
supports: Exclude qualifying mapped open water from terrestrial pluvial scores, class areas and exposure counts; retain it as a separate excluded category
does_not_support: A calibrated separation of all fluvial and pluvial flooding

available_data_interpretation.dataset: Municipal 1 m DTM; 5 m mean terrain derivatives
available_data_interpretation.can_support: Terrain shape, geometric depression storage, modelled downhill contributing area and slope; native 1 m inspection.
available_data_interpretation.cannot_support: Known vertical accuracy, rainfall intensity, water depth in a specified event, current buildings/kerbs/culverts, pipe hydraulics or observed flood occurrence. A 1 m grid does not establish 1 m accuracy.

available_data_interpretation.can_support: Location and recorded existing/planned/open status of archived linework; overlap for inspection.
available_data_interpretation.cannot_support: Current drain coverage, storm inlet locations, connectivity, invert levels, pipe capacity, condition, blockage or reduction of flood susceptibility. Planned routes cannot be assumed operational.

available_data_interpretation.can_support: Recorded green-area context and comparison of overlaps.
available_data_interpretation.cannot_support: Measured impervious fraction, infiltration rate, soil saturation or stormwater storage. Do not lower a flood score simply because a cell intersects a green polygon.

available_data_interpretation.can_support: Counts and locations of records overlapping selected terrain screening classes.
available_data_interpretation.cannot_support: Number of unique physical assets, service importance, asset value, damage susceptibility, populations or drainage capacity. Source rows may represent multiple surveyed points along a structure.

available_data_interpretation.can_support: A hidden 5 m exclusion mask for qualifying mapped water footprints. Excluded water receives no score; land scores and original terrain factors remain unchanged.
available_data_interpretation.cannot_support: Water-edge accuracy at the date of a storm, complete river coverage, bridge-deck classification or protection of surrounding land from river flooding.

historical_evidence_leads.title: Sofia Municipality: situation report at 07:00, 16 June 2023
historical_evidence_leads.event_date_precision: Overnight before the morning report; not an exact timestamp for each location.
reported_locations: Southern arc of Sofia Ring Road
historical_evidence_leads.finding: The municipality reports temporary road closures from ponding at the southern ring road and Lion's Bridge tunnels, plus overnight inundation/other storm reports in named districts. It cites a citywide range of 40–70 mm of rain by midnight from NIMH.
historical_evidence_leads.use: Qualitative historical evidence and a lead for requesting exact incident locations and times. Broad district mentions include mixed storm impacts and are not complete flood footprints.

historical_evidence_leads.title: NIMH Monthly Hydrometeorological Bulletin, October 2025
historical_evidence_leads.publisher: National Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology, Bulgaria
historical_evidence_leads.locator: Printed page 11, especially dangerous phenomena, 27 October
historical_evidence_leads.finding: NIMH reports a flooded Sofia intersection disrupting several tram lines and a measured 24-hour rainfall total of 42.9 mm.
historical_evidence_leads.use: Independent evidence that rainfall-related urban disruption occurred; identify the intersection and obtain incident details before spatial comparison. The total is not street-level rainfall or a short-duration intensity.

recommended_implementation_contract.map_label: Pluvial flood screening — relative terrain susceptibility
factor_layers: Geometric depression fill depth (m; not flood depth)
recommended_implementation_contract.ranking: Any per-cell composite, percentile normalization, thresholds, weights, mask or high-priority class is an analyst-defined screening choice unless separately calibrated. Display its formula and factor values. Do not label this TCI or TWI unless the published algorithm and units are actually implemented.
recommended_implementation_contract.sensitivity: Compare at least depth-focused, flow-focused and balanced analyst scenarios; report class/rank changes and stable overlap. Scenario agreement is internal sensitivity, not validation or confidence probability.
recommended_implementation_contract.exposure: Show infrastructure record counts and route lengths overlapping priority terrain separately, retaining source dates and status. Do not convert these to losses or use sewer density as capacity.
recommended_implementation_contract.unknowns: Mask missing raster inputs and flag boundary-influenced flow; zero is not an acceptable replacement for unknown. Outside the screen does not mean safe.
recommended_implementation_contract.hydrology: D8 routing and fill-depth describe simplified surface topography. Larger contributing area can identify river valleys as well as rainfall flow paths; do not automatically identify either as a pluvial flood event.
recommended_implementation_contract.minimum_validation_for_upgrade: Geolocated independently recorded pluvial flood events with dates and negative/coverage evidence; local sub-hourly rainfall or IDF data; drainage and culvert inventory/capacity/condition; verified terrain accuracy and current building/road representation. Use event calibration and held-out validation before probability, return-period, depth or loss claims.
